claims.text: The cast CrMnFeCoNi alloy has a single-phase FCC microstructure.
The CrMnFeCoNi alloy has a single-phase FCC equilibrium region from about 750°C to 1320°C.
At lower temperatures, CrMnFeCoNi can decompose to include sigma and BCC phases.
Testing from room temperature to about 600°C avoids the lower-temperature phase decomposition of CrMnFeCoNi.
The alloy should be modified with approximately 5–10 atomic percent Al.
Adding 5–10 atomic percent Al to CrMnFeCoNi will retain a stable single-phase FCC structure.
Atomic disorder will be maintained after partial substitution of the constituent elements by Al.
Substitution of heavier constituent elements with Al will decrease the alloy density.
Al substitution will preserve or enhance the strength and ductility of CrMnFeCoNi.
Retention of the FCC structure will provide a plastic-deformation pathway without significant phase instability over the target temperature range.
Al-alloyed CrMnFeCoNi will have approximately 10–20% lower density than unalloyed CrMnFeCoNi.
Al-alloyed CrMnFeCoNi will maintain or improve its mechanical properties from room temperature to about 600°C.
Higher-temperature exposure may compromise phase stability and comprehensive performance.
Excessive Al addition may compromise phase stability and degrade comprehensive performance.
The optimal Al concentration for balancing low density and phase stability has not been established.
Long-term cyclic-loading and environmental behavior of the proposed Al-alloyed material remains unevaluated.

contradictions.description: The proposed room-temperature-to-600°C window is said to avoid lower-temperature decomposition and retain a stable FCC phase, while the conditions themselves acknowledge lower-temperature sigma-phase formation. The cited record places the calculated single-phase FCC stability interval at about 750–1320°C, so the stated rationale for the selected window is internally inconsistent.

The boundary suggests that moving above about 600°C may compromise phase stability, whereas the cited base-alloy evidence identifies approximately 750–1320°C as the single-phase FCC equilibrium interval. The statement may conceivably apply to an Al-modified alloy, but no Al-specific evidence is supplied.
